content.value_statement: Turn ambiguous feature requests into structured product specifications that align design, engineering, and review. This skill defines user-visible behavior, scope, references, open questions, and handoff details in a consistent PRODUCT.md format.
actual_capabilities: Create a PRODUCT.md document for a substantial user-facing feature.
Organize feature context, behavior, scope, and open questions.
Capture Linear, GitHub, and Figma references when the user provides them.
Define user-visible states, edge cases, and interaction details in plain language.
Apply a consistent structure that supports implementation and review handoff.
limitations: It does not implement the feature or produce a companion technical design.
It cannot verify requirements, links, or designs that the user does not provide.
It does not replace product, design, engineering, or accessibility review.
It is tailored to the documented Warp PRODUCT.md conventions.

use_cases.title: Product discovery brief
use_cases.description: Convert an early feature idea into a focused behavior specification with explicit scope and unresolved decisions.

use_cases.title: Design handoff
use_cases.description: Record user flows, states, and Figma references so designers and engineers share the same expected behavior.

use_cases.title: Engineering planning
use_cases.description: Give implementers a review-ready PRODUCT.md that clarifies edge cases without prescribing unnecessary implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Start a product spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRODUCT.md for this feature: [feature idea]. Ask only for missing context that blocks a useful specification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn a rough idea into a structured first draft.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify feature behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this feature request as a PRODUCT.md. Define the user problem, expected behavior, scope boundaries, states, and open questions: [request].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: remove ambiguity before implementation begins.

prompt_templates.title: Use project references
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRODUCT.md for [feature]. Use this ticket or issue: [link]. Include this design reference if relevant: [Figma link]. Preserve only confirmed context and list unresolved decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine approved references with explicit uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Review a specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this PRODUCT.md for ambiguous behavior, missing edge cases, scope creep, and unsupported assumptions. Return a revised specification plus a concise list of open questions: [specification].
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: make a draft ready for cross-functional review.

output_examples.input: Add a command palette that opens with a keyboard shortcut and supports recent commands.
output_examples.output: A PRODUCT.md outline covering the user problem, invocation behavior, search states, empty results, keyboard navigation, scope exclusions, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Feature request with a Linear ticket and Figma link.
output_examples.output: A review-ready specification that places the ticket and design reference in the appropriate context, separates confirmed behavior from open questions, and avoids invented requirements.

output_examples.input: Ambiguous request to improve tab management.
output: A focused behavior section for tab actions and states.
Explicit scope boundaries and unresolved product decisions.
A concise handoff suitable for design and engineering review.

best_practices: Provide the user problem, feature context, and known constraints before drafting.
Separate confirmed behavior from open questions and assumptions.
Review the specification with product, design, and engineering stakeholders before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not invent ticket details, design decisions, metrics, or requirements.
Do not hide unresolved behavior inside vague implementation language.
Do not use the product specification as a substitute for technical design or test planning.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a structured PRODUCT.md specification for a substantial user-facing feature.

faq.question: Does it implement the feature?
faq.answer: No. It documents expected behavior and scope for later design and engineering work.

faq.question: Can it use Linear or GitHub references?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include ticket or issue identifiers and links when the user provides them.

faq.question: Can it use Figma designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include a provided Figma link and clearly note when no mock exists.

faq.question: Will it invent missing requirements?
faq.answer: It should identify missing information as open questions instead of presenting assumptions as facts.

faq.question: Who benefits most from the output?
faq.answer: Product managers, designers, and engineers who need a shared description of feature behavior.
